rule.description: A concrete I/O backend is wired through one fat StreamOps function-pointer table bundling input, output, positioning and lifecycle capabilities, and must fill capabilities it does not implement with no-op stubs; every owner depends on capabilities it never uses.

checks.description: Detect a fat StreamOps interface and each installed StreamOps table that fills three or more slots with no-op stubs, so each owner is forced to depend on capabilities it never uses.
checks.detected_relation: I/O backend -> fat StreamOps interface bundling unrelated read/write/position/lifecycle capabilities the backend stubs out
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: A single interface exceeds the dependency boundary of every concrete backend: read-only sources stub the output and positioning slots, write-only sinks stub the input and positioning slots, and the diagnostic reporter cannot close the sink it does not own.

matches.evidence: struct StreamOps bundles read/unread/eof/emitv/putstr/flush/tell/seek/close in one definition that every backend must complete.
file_stream_ops (FILE-backed input) installs noop_emitv, noop_putstr, noop_flush, noop_tell, noop_seek for capabilities a read-only source never uses.
string_stream_ops (in-memory input) installs noop_emitv, noop_putstr, noop_flush, noop_tell, noop_seek for capabilities a read-only source never uses.
output_stream_ops (assembly output sink) installs noop_read, noop_unread, noop_eof, noop_tell, noop_seek for capabilities a write-only sink never uses.
err_stream_ops (stderr diagnostic sink) installs noop_read, noop_unread, noop_eof, noop_tell, noop_seek, noop_close for capabilities a stderr writer never uses and must not invoke.
